programme.title: American Loggers
programme.desc: In this series, we meet the Pelletier family - nine brothers who have to deal with the harsh nature, equipment failures and everyday squabbles so that their company, Pelletier Inc., can function smoothly.This company is the embodiment of the American dream.50 years ago, Gerald Pelletier founded it on his own, with one truck and $100.Currently, his sons run a large corporation that employs dozens of workers and uses hundreds of machines to cut down thousands of hectares of forest. It's snowing in Maine.For most people this is bad news, but for lumberjacks - quite the opposite.The Pelletiers call snow "white gold" because it allows them to pull logs out of the forest faster.A new driver, Dana Noble, reports for work.He is assigned to truck number 71, called "cursed" because it has already overturned twice.During the first ride, Dana gets stuck on an icy road.Meanwhile, lumberjacks with telling nicknames: Bonebreaker, Playboy and Jason Przyjemniaczek set off from Millinocket to the sawmill.Soon, certain events force them to return.Jeff Pelletier loses his temper when he breaks a plowshare while clearing the area.

programme.title: American Loggers
programme.desc: In this series, we meet the Pelletier family - nine brothers who have to deal with the harsh nature, equipment failures and everyday squabbles so that their company, Pelletier Inc., can function smoothly.This company is the embodiment of the American dream.50 years ago, Gerald Pelletier founded it on his own, with one truck and $100.Currently, his sons run a large corporation that employs dozens of workers and uses hundreds of machines to cut down thousands of hectares of forest. The area is covered with a thirty-centimeter layer of snow.This means big problems for the family business.At sub-zero temperatures, equipment gets trapped in the forest and trucks get stuck in snowdrifts.Wayne Pelletier wastes an entire day when a frozen trailer rim disintegrates and strands him on the Trans-Canada Highway.And on the icy Ladd Hill Road, driver Lester Dube, known as the Red Baron, recalls his brush with death.Just as he is telling a story about his miraculous survival, he loses control of the vehicle and almost drives into a stream.Despite equipment failure and many worries, lumberjacks and drivers deliver 5,400 yards of wood to the sawmill - this is a record week for the company.
